changes.before: WHEN retained records reach their configured bound, the authority SHALL reclaim only records whose safety obligations are preserved by retained proofs and replay floors, or explicitly refuse new admission while preserving unresolved and cleanup obligations.
changes.after: WHEN retained records reach their configured bound, the authority SHALL reclaim only records whose obligations remain protected by proofs and replay floors, or report distinct capacity refusal while preserving unresolved and cleanup obligations until proof-safe reclamation permits admission.

changes.before: No age-based deletion of Unknown, cleanup, issuance/revocation authority or replay floors. A presentation close/restart is not proof-safe reclamation.
changes.after: No age-based deletion of Unknown, cleanup, issuance/revocation authority or replay floors. A presentation close/restart is not proof-safe reclamation. Capacity refusal is distinct from the original operation outcome and clears when proof-safe reclamation is possible. Scope replay floors retire only through authority-certified scope retirement or equivalent retained proof.

before.name: Expired replay after compaction
before.given: A settled reclaimable record and retained replay floor
before.when: Compaction completes and its old identity returns
before.then: No mutation occurs and defined expired disposition is recorded

before.name: Unknown and late cleanup
before.given: Capacity pressure, Unknown request and outstanding consumer fence
before.when: Diagnostics rotate and matching late receipt arrives
before.then: Unresolved/cleanup obligations remain reconciled and charged storage is not freed prematurely

after.name: Expired replay after compaction
after.given: A settled reclaimable record and retained replay floor
after.when: Compaction completes and its old identity returns
after.then: no mutation occurs; expired or retention disposition is distinct from definitive refusal of the original operation, and retained Unknown remains unchanged

after.name: Unknown and late cleanup
after.given: Capacity pressure, Unknown request and outstanding consumer fence
after.when: Diagnostics rotate and matching late receipt arrives
after.then: Unresolved/cleanup obligations remain reconciled and charged storage is not freed prematurely

changes.before: Caching/indexing is an implementation option after profiling. Cache keys include native dependency/output/publication revisions; stale cached data grants no authority.
changes.after: Caching/indexing is an implementation option after profiling. Cache keys include native dependency/output/publication revisions; stale cached data grants no authority. Enable an optimization only after the frozen workload comparison shows an accepted benefit; equivalence alone does not justify adopting it.

before.when: Taskbar groups are derived

before.then: New identities govern derivation and action eligibility; stale family/preview authority does not survive

after.name: Unchanged dependency
after.given: Pointer events with unchanged scene/query/policy revisions
after.when: Taskbar groups are derived
after.then: output equals the uncached oracle under the correct dependency revision; recomputation and whole-process resource results are measured separately for the adoption decision

after.name: Identity reuse race
after.given: Cached retired family incarnation
after.when: Same label appears under new lifetime/incarnation during query change
after.then: New identities govern derivation and action eligibility; stale family/preview authority does not survive

changes.before: Explicit partial-observation/stuttering abstraction; compare actual commands and resources as well as model state. Bounded sampling/trace validation is not an exhaustive proof.
changes.after: Explicit partial-observation/stuttering abstraction; compare actual commands and resources as well as model state. Bounded sampling/trace validation is not an exhaustive proof. Every concrete state and command field is listed as mapped or explicitly reviewed quotient/stutter/ghost-only; an unlisted field fails coverage. Quotients preserve authentication/binding identity, clock/deadline and outcome meaning; reviewed opaque-nonce renaming is allowed without erasing those relations.

after: ELM-ADOPT-005 Equal final state with incorrect effect order

after.given: a runtime mutant drops an Unknown reservation or changes an undeclared field
after.when: abstraction coverage and coupled replay run
after.then: verification fails at that field rather than silently observing only the visible model

changes.before: Narrow module-owned typed events, effects and identity domains; native authenticates context. Do not mandate a new language, framework, giant event type or incompatible wire change.
changes.after: Narrow module-owned typed events, effects and identity domains; native authenticates context. Do not mandate a new language, framework, giant event type or incompatible wire change. Terminal Refused requires exact authenticated native evidence or a validated definitive unsent certificate. Historical proof admission follows its explicit recovery contract.

before.name: Exact receipt
before.given: a validated receipt for one request/incarnation
before.when: the typed outcome is reduced
before.then: only the exact transaction settles and wire encoding remains unchanged

before.name: Foreign input
before.given: a malformed or foreign-binding payload
before.when: boundary validation runs
before.then: no admitted event or mutation is produced and correlated refusal is retained

after.name: Exact receipt
after.given: a validated receipt for one request/incarnation
after.when: the typed outcome is reduced
after.then: only the exact transaction settles and wire encoding remains unchanged

after.name: Foreign input
after.given: a malformed, untrusted or unauthorized payload that fails boundary admission
after.when: boundary validation runs
after.then: no admitted event, native mutation or transaction settlement is produced; only a bounded allowlisted rejection diagnostic is retained, with no fabricated Refused outcome

after.name: authenticated-historical-reconciliation
after.given: an exact authenticated historical receipt for a retained obligation and its declared reconciliation route
after.when: it arrives after frontend replacement
after.then: only the historical obligation may settle; the receipt grants no authority to the replacement binding and renews no deadline

changes.before: WHEN a native effect depends on another effect's completion, the controller SHALL admit the dependent request only after the matching native committed receipt satisfies the recorded prerequisite.
changes.after: WHEN a native effect depends on a prerequisite, the controller SHALL admit its request only after matching authenticated evidence satisfies that operation's protocol-specific prerequisite, while native authority revalidates the dependency at commit.

changes.before: Register every implied native request; preserve child effects. Cmd.batch does not sequence dependent results. Independent actions need not wait for unrelated dependencies.
changes.after: Register every implied native request; preserve child effects. Cmd.batch does not sequence dependent results. Independent actions need not wait for unrelated dependencies. Native revalidates prerequisite incarnation, generation and dependency revision. Preview drain/release/presentation require their own evidence; a window Committed receipt cannot substitute.

changes.before: WHEN an authenticated protocol event is admitted, each participant SHALL follow the declared actor-specific legal transitions and outcome reachability for that protocol version, preserving exact correlation and stable proof identities.
changes.after: WHEN a protocol event is received, each participant SHALL admit it only under the declared actor-specific transitions, version and outcome reachability with exact correlation; otherwise it SHALL reject it without authority, ownership or settlement effect and retain a bounded rejection diagnostic.

changes.before: Metadata and clock/queue instrumentation; frontend timers feedback only; vector clocks unnecessary.
changes.after: Metadata and clock/queue instrumentation; frontend timers may provide feedback or fail-closed withdrawal of unsent local intent, but cannot authorize, extend, settle or time native work or substitute for native original deadlines. Vector clocks are unnecessary.

changes.before: Stable bounded outcome/reason catalog and actionable localized text. Unknown remains perceivable. Unknown reason within a validated Refused class may use generic refusal text; unknown schema/outcome cannot fabricate Refused.
changes.after: Stable bounded outcome/reason catalog and actionable, reviewed text from a catalog that supports localization. Unknown remains perceivable. Unknown reason within a validated Refused class may use generic refusal text; unknown schema/outcome cannot fabricate Refused. Supporting localization does not add a translation release gate.

before.name: ERR-02-01
before.given: bar and popup projections on two outputs with stable focus
before.when: the same refusal receipt is delivered repeatedly and a popup recreates
before.then: one eligible announcement occurs and recovery detail remains reachable.

before.name: ERR-02-02
before.given: Unknown was announced and the original deadline has elapsed
before.when: a valid late correlated receipt settles knowledge
before.then: a distinct policy-eligible update is exposed without restarting the effect or changing its deadline; foreign-epoch receipts produce no such update.

after.name: ERR-02-01
after.given: bar and popup projections on two outputs with stable focus
after.when: the same refusal receipt is delivered repeatedly and a popup recreates
after.then: one eligible announcement occurs and recovery detail remains reachable.

after.name: ERR-02-02
after.given: Unknown was announced and the original deadline has elapsed
after.when: a valid late correlated receipt settles knowledge
after.then: a distinct policy-eligible update is exposed without restarting the effect or changing its deadline; unauthenticated, unrelated or unauthorized receipts cause no update, while exact authenticated historical evidence may reconcile retained Unknown through the declared recovery route

changes.before: Allowlist excludes secrets, draft content, pixels, raw port bodies, titles/arguments/paths by default. Bounded lost-record counters. Diagnostics saturation cannot block native control/cleanup or compact durable authority.
changes.after: Secrets, credentials, draft contents and captured pixels are always excluded from ordinary diagnostics under ELM-DEL-017. Raw port bodies, titles, arguments and paths are also excluded by this ordinary allowlist. A different scoped mode requires a separate reviewed contract and is outside this draft. Retention/loss counters remain bounded. Saturation cannot block native control/cleanup or compact durable authority.

changes.before: unrestricted verbose logs simplify one incident at privacy/resource cost; aggregate-only metrics lose sequence context. Cost: event schema, producer audits and saturation tests. A ring buffer and separate counters are possible implementations, not mandated architecture. Validation: sensitive canaries across nested values and error strings; resource saturation, failure to write and malformed events preserve controller decisions. Measure log-rate, whole-process CPU/wakeups/memory, export cost and retention against `elm-performance/spec.md` ELM-PER obligations; the performance owner freezes numeric limits from P0 workloads before acceptance.
changes.after: unrestricted verbose logs simplify one incident at privacy/resource cost; aggregate-only metrics lose sequence context. Cost: event schema, producer audits and saturation tests. A ring buffer and separate counters are possible implementations, not mandated architecture. Validation: sensitive canaries across nested values and error strings; resource saturation, failure to write and malformed events preserve controller decisions. Measure log-rate, whole-process CPU/wakeups/memory, export cost and retention against `elm-performance/spec.md` ELM-QA-021/023 and ELM-REV-020/021; the performance owner freezes numeric limits from P0 workloads before acceptance. Measure under the actual ELM-QA-021/023 and ELM-REV-020/021 budget contract.

before.name: ERR-04-01
before.given: an admitted effect and crash before durable settlement
before.when: a fresh epoch receives a coherent snapshot
before.then: availability may recover while the previous effect remains unconfirmed and is never replayed.

before.name: ERR-04-02
before.given: a storage-full recovery failure and matching-looking geometry from a replacement incarnation
before.when: reconciliation is attempted
before.then: geometry alone cannot clear the historical reservation, no new dependent effect is admitted and the original recovery deadline remains enforced.

after.name: ERR-04-01
after.given: an admitted effect and crash before durable settlement
after.when: a fresh epoch receives a coherent snapshot
after.then: availability may recover while the previous effect remains unconfirmed and is never replayed.

after.name: ERR-04-02
after.given: a storage-full recovery failure and matching-looking geometry from a replacement incarnation
after.when: reconciliation is attempted
after.then: geometry alone cannot clear the historical reservation, no new dependent effect is admitted and each affected operation's original deadline is unchanged and is not renewed by recovery.

changes.before: WHEN a presentation publication changes while a shell scope retains focus, the host SHALL preserve the focused surviving control identity, reject activation captured for retired or changed-scope identities, and apply the frozen eligible fallback only when that control is no longer eligible.
changes.after: WHILE a shell focus scope is open, the host SHALL preserve an eligible focused control through unrelated publications and dispatch admitted keyboard or assistive activation only to that native AT-exposed identity, rejecting retired or changed-scope targets and applying the frozen fallback when focus becomes ineligible.

changes.before: Publication/lease/incarnation captured at press remains authoritative at release. Preserve a surviving focus identity across unrelated changes; explicit eligible fallback only on removal. Keyed DOM is an implementation choice. Admitted keyboard activation must equal the native AT-exposed focused identity, not merely a selected row.
changes.after: Publication, lease and incarnation captured at press remain authoritative at release. Preserve the surviving focused identity while eligible under the frozen per-surface policy; disabled-but-focusable controls remain focused when030 allows it, otherwise apply the declared fallback. Selection is distinct from focus. Keyed DOM is an implementation choice.

before.name: SOL04-01-scenario-1
before.given: Close is focused while another row is selected
before.when: an unrelated catalog publication arrives
before.then: Close keeps focus and the next activation invokes only Close

before.name: SOL04-01-scenario-2
before.given: an activation press belongs to a window incarnation and lease
before.when: that incarnation retires and the row position is reused before release
before.then: release dispatches no replacement action and eligible fallback remains reachable

after.name: SOL04-01-scenario-1
after.given: Close is focused while another row is selected
after.when: an unrelated catalog publication arrives
after.then: Close keeps focus and the next activation invokes only Close

after.name: SOL04-01-scenario-2
after.given: an activation press belongs to a window incarnation and lease
after.when: that incarnation retires and the row position is reused before release
after.then: release dispatches no replacement action and eligible fallback remains reachable

after.name: focus-without-publication
after.given: Close has keyboard/native AT focus while another row is selected
after.when: Enter or Space is admitted without an intervening publication
after.then: only Close is invoked, no window intent is dispatched and selection cannot override focused identity

changes.before: Control semantics plus actual native bridge required. Announcement ownership is separately ELM-ADOPT-012; multiple read-only status regions do not establish a single AT announcement. Keep the visible stable control label as the accessible name; expose transient state and action descriptions separately, within the frozen per-control naming policy.
changes.after: Control semantics plus actual native bridge required. Announcement ownership is separately ELM-ADOPT-012; multiple read-only status regions do not establish a single AT announcement. Keep the visible stable control label as the accessible name; expose transient state and action descriptions separately, within the frozen per-control naming policy. Verify cross-surface relationships in the native AT tree; DOM-local relationships do not automatically cross WebView documents.

before.name: SOL04-02-scenario-1
before.given: bar and popup show the same pending operation
before.when: the matching refusal arrives twice
before.then: one relevant refusal is announced, both projections show the same outcome, and focus remains on the user's control

before.name: SOL04-02-scenario-2
before.given: a preview image has retired while its restore control survives
before.when: AT explores the control
before.then: source state and supported action are available without an actionable image object or stale-incarnation activation

after.name: SOL04-02-scenario-1
after.given: bar and popup show the same pending operation
after.when: the matching refusal arrives twice
after.then: both projections expose the same refusal state for the same control identity and focus remains on the user's control; announcement count follows ELM-ADOPT-012

after.name: SOL04-02-scenario-2
after.given: a preview image has retired while its restore control survives
after.when: AT explores the control
after.then: source state and supported action are available without an actionable image object or stale-incarnation activation

after.name: stable-name-state-change
after.given: a single-window group whose visible identity label is unchanged becomes active or pending
after.when: native AT re-reads the control
after.then: the accessible name remains aligned with the same visible label while state/description changes under the frozen naming policy

changes.before: WHEN a shell action is unavailable or its outcome is unresolved, the shell SHALL expose the correlated reason and safe next step, retain eligible focus and independent controls, and avoid queuing or automatically replaying a rejected or Unknown action.
changes.after: WHEN a shell action is unavailable or unresolved, the shell SHALL expose the correlated reason and safe next step, retain eligible focus and controls outside its dependency domain, and never queue, defer or automatically replay input not accepted in that state or a rejected or Unknown action.

changes.before: Unrelated refresh must not collapse a valid picker or disable unrelated actions. Repeated clicks during pending have truthful outcome under the interruption policy; no announcement storm.
changes.after: Unrelated refresh means an unchanged declared family/target dependency domain and must preserve a valid picker/focus. Do not require concurrent native transactions. Repeated input during Pending follows INTERACTION.md feedback policy and ELM-UI-015; no second intent or announcement storm.

before.name: SOL04-05-scenario-1
before.given: a minimized generic application family is selected
before.when: activation is refused natively
before.then: it is not shown as restored, the reason and next action are reachable, and its preserved identity remains selected

before.name: SOL04-05-scenario-2
before.given: an operation has Unknown disposition and guidance was dismissed
before.when: the user opens help or recovery with the keyboard
before.then: guidance is available without resetting the desktop and reconciliation creates no automatic repeated mutation

after.name: SOL04-05-scenario-1
after.given: a minimized generic application family is selected
after.when: activation is refused natively
after.then: it is not shown as restored, the reason and next action are reachable, and its preserved identity remains selected

after.name: SOL04-05-scenario-2
after.given: an operation has Unknown disposition and guidance was dismissed
after.when: the user opens help or recovery with the keyboard
after.then: guidance is available without resetting the desktop and reconciliation creates no automatic repeated mutation

after.name: unrelated-observation-refresh
after.given: a picker is open for a family
after.when: an unrelated observation refresh completes with that family's dependency revision unchanged
after.then: picker identity and focus persist and no new intent is emitted

after.name: same-control-during-pending
after.given: a native operation is Pending for a control
after.when: the same control is activated again
after.then: no second intent is emitted; one truthful not-accepted result is exposed under the frozen feedback policy without repeated announcement or later replay

before.name: Observation storm with cancellation
before.given: preview queues are saturated within frozen byte and item bounds
before.when: new observations and a cancellation arrive
before.then: only semantically replaceable observations coalesce; cancellation and all retirement receipts remain deliverable in order

before.name: Close during producer reservation
before.given: a producer owns a reservation and the picker closes
before.when: a late producer result arrives
before.then: demand remains cancelled and the existing owner receives cleanup; no new capture is admitted until capacity is legitimately released

after.name: Observation storm with cancellation
after.given: preview queues are saturated within frozen byte and item bounds
after.when: new observations and a cancellation arrive
after.then: only semantically replaceable observations coalesce; cancellation and all retirement receipts remain deliverable in order

after.name: Close during producer reservation
after.given: a producer owns a reservation and the picker closes
after.when: a late producer result arrives
after.then: the closed demand remains cancelled and its existing owner/cleanup stays recorded; another authorized demand may use only independently available eligible capacity, never the held reservation before matching release

changes.before: WHILE preview demand remains authorized, WHEN a newer content revision arrives during outstanding capture, the provider SHALL retain bounded latest-content demand and service it after eligible capacity returns, without admitting work after demand closes or authority revokes.
changes.after: WHILE authorized preview demand persists, WHEN tracked source content advances during outstanding capture, the provider SHALL retain bounded latest-revision demand and service it under the frozen pacing policy after eligible capacity returns, admitting none after closure or revocation.

changes.before: No forced allocation while backpressured/exhausted. Follow-up is a genuine new native-scoped request with its own original issued clock, not renewal of expired work. Control/retirement events are lossless.
changes.after: No forced allocation while backpressured/exhausted. Follow-up is a genuine new native-scoped request with its own original issued clock, not renewal of expired work. Control/retirement events are lossless. Pacing/refresh is frozen in the existing budget matrix before qualification; continuous change cannot create unbounded back-to-back capture. Latest revision is limited to native-tracked coverage, currently root-surface commits only; no subsurface/family fidelity expansion.

before.name: final-content-while-busy
before.given: one admitted capture and multiple newer same-source revisions while visible demand persists
before.when: the first job terminates and capacity returns
before.then: bounded demand selects the latest valid revision without losing the final update or extending the first job deadline

before.name: close-or-lock-before-followup
before.given: a pending latest-content update
before.when: demand closes, lock/revocation occurs or source identity changes before admission
before.then: no unauthorized follow-up capture is admitted; existing jobs and cleanup obligations remain accounted

after.name: final-content-while-busy
after.given: one admitted capture and multiple newer same-source revisions while visible demand persists
after.when: the first job terminates and capacity returns
after.then: bounded demand selects the latest valid revision without losing the final update or extending the first job deadline

after.name: close-or-lock-before-followup
after.given: a pending latest-content update
after.when: demand closes, lock/revocation occurs or source identity changes before admission
after.then: no unauthorized follow-up capture is admitted; existing jobs and cleanup obligations remain accounted

after.name: continuous-change-and-final-revision
after.given: authorized visible demand, continuously changing tracked content and eventually available eligible capacity
after.when: the provider runs and then content change stops
after.then: capture follows the frozen pacing policy, the final tracked revision is serviced when eligible, and presentation impact is measured under026 with no original deadline renewal

changes.before: WHEN a supported shell action becomes disabled, the shell SHALL retain its declared position, expose its reason and disabled state, and follow the frozen per-surface navigation policy without dispatching it through pointer, keyboard or accessibility activation.
changes.after: WHEN a supported shell action becomes disabled, the shell SHALL retain its declared position, expose disabled state and any reason required by the frozen per-surface policy, and follow that navigation policy without dispatching it through pointer, keyboard or accessibility activation.
